newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar ends weaker in steady trading.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar ends weaker in steady trading.

text.p: * The Canadian dollar ended weaker in moderate trading on Thursday at C$1.3612 (US$0.7347) from Wednesday's close at C$1.3597 (US$0.7355), traders said.
* They said a domestic interest to sell buy U.S. dollars, coupled with weaker bonds, poor retail sales numbers and technical factors, pushed the Canadian dollar weaker.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast a 0.7 percent rise in retail sales in December after November's 0.9 percent rise.
A break through the key technical point of C$1.3600 (US$0.7352) prompted a round of selling, traders said.
And weaker Canadian bonds also took some strength out of the currency, they said. Canada's 30-year bond fell C$0.85 to C$112.90 to yield 6.926 percent.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar slipped to 1.2360 marks from Wednesday's 1.2478 marks and fell to 90.12 yen from 91.54 yen.
